newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt mkts close little changed after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt mkts close little changed after quiet day.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
* Trade subdued in short end after recent rally
* Bid tone remains, currency still strong
* Long end looks to Friday's U.S. payrolls data
New Zealand debt markets closed little changed on Wednesday after a quiet session, although the short end remained well bid in light of the strong currency.
"It was a very quiet day. There was a good move down yesterday on the back of the currency, but today it's just sat really, taking a rest," a bill trader said.
However, he said there was still a positive tone in the marketplace. "I think so, it could pick up a couple of points, but not too far."

In the bond market, dealers said trade had been very light with little action, although the 02/00 yield fell one basis point. "There's a real summer slow-down feel about it," said one dealer. "The focus I think has pretty swiftly swung to Friday's (U.S.) nonfarm payrolls."
The important U.S. employment data is expected to direct the bond market until the release of domestic inflation data on January 17.
